prose.title: The Chrysaorian Revolt
prose.summary: The Karian cities of Kaunos, Antiocheia-Alabanda and Stratonikeia break away and form the Chrysaorian League. At the start of the campaign Kaunos belongs to the Ptolemaic Empire and the other two to the Seleucid Empire. The revolt can break out early under Rhodian rule, and it happens by itself at turn 102 (245 BC) at the latest.
prose.breaks_away_from: whoever holds Kaunos, Antiocheia-Alabanda and Stratonikeia (at the start, the Ptolemaic Empire and the Seleucid Empire)
prose.who_it_can_happen_to: It can happen in any campaign, whether the three cities are held by a human or by the AI.
what_sets_it_off: One of the three cities rebels on its own after Rhodes has held at least two of the three at the start of more than 10 turns in total (they need not be in a row).
If it has not happened before, the revolt breaks out automatically at the start of turn 102 (245 BC).
what_happens: Kaunos, Antiocheia-Alabanda and Stratonikeia all rebel, whoever owns them.
All three cities pass to the Chrysaorian League, a faction that does not exist at the start of the campaign.

Each city gets a normal-strength garrison drawn from Akontistai, Greek Slingers, Greek Archers, Greek Peltasts, Karian Hoplites, Karian Thureophoroi, Karian Leukaspides Swordsmen, Karian Light Infantry, Karian Heavy Infantry, Prodromoi and Xystophoroi.
The Chrysaorian League receives 10000 denarii when Kaunos joins it.
The revolt happens only once per campaign.
prose.playing_as_the_rebels: If the human player held at least one of the three cities at the start of the turn in which the revolt broke out, the message 'The Chrysaorian League declares independence!' appears at the start of the next turn and offers the chance to take over the Chrysaorian League. Accepting switches the player to the League and adds a government building in Stratonikeia, Kaunos and Antiocheia-Alabanda; declining changes nothing. A player who held none of the three cities gets no offer. The Chrysaorian League is a playable faction.
